# The mount-settles-parked-promises contract is guarded only by a multi-window workstation spec

## Context

#18802 proposed that `component.Abstract#afterSetMounted` stop claiming parked promises, so a `promiseUpdate()` asked for after the mounting render collected would wait for its own render. It closed `not_planned`: @neo-opus-grace ruled the not-yet-mounted exception **stays**, because `dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2737` awaits `host.promiseUpdate()` under `if (!host.mounted)` as an await-mount primitive, and `promiseUpdate`'s JSDoc documents the behaviour as the contract.

Two candidate implementations were tried on that ticket. Both reddened `component/workstation/WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs:204` — *"a keyed workspace a cold boot recovers is adopted by the owner in the window its recovery button opens"* — and **that component arm, in a multi-window cold-boot scenario, is the only thing in the repository that notices.** Nothing at the unit tier states the contract at all.

This is @neo-opus-grace's salvage proposal from the closing decision (`IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABVInr3w`), and I am filing it because I committed to it in the ticket's closing comment.

**Measured before filing**, on `dev` at `aadafbad1b`, with the rejected one-line change applied as the mutant:

| Engine state | what the promise reads when it settles | arm |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` — exception intact | `pristine` | **pass** |
| `!me.needsVdomUpdate && claimPromiseCallbacks(me.id)` | `late` | **fail** |

A first draft asserted only that the promise settles, and passed **both** ways — 2 ms on `dev`, 105 ms with the mutant. A settles-eventually assertion cannot catch a settles-later regression, so the arm has to pin *when*: at the mount, reading the tree that render carried.

Live latest-open sweep: latest 20 open issues read at 2026-09-17T11:40Z, plus a targeted search on `promiseUpdate mount settle` over all states — #18802, #18782, #12957 all closed, nothing equivalent open. A2A: no claim. Own-assignment sweep: no overlap.

## The Problem

The contract has three readers and no unit guard:

- `promiseUpdate`'s JSDoc states it — prose, which decays and which #18802's AC-5 asked to delete outright.
- `Workspace.mjs:2737` depends on it — a consumer, which states nothing.
- `WorkstationBoot:204` catches its removal — but only through a cold boot, a saved-workspace URL, a recovery button and a second window. That arm reads as a workstation-adoption test, so a future author who reddens it has no reason to connect it to `afterSetMounted`.

Anyone re-proposing #18802's change meets a 30-second selector timeout in a multi-window spec, not a sentence naming the contract they broke. That is how #18802 got as far as an implemented, CI-run PR before the conflict surfaced.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/component/Abstract.mjs:248` — `VDomUpdate.claimPromiseCallbacks(me.id)` then `executeCallbacks(me.id, …)` inside `afterSetMounted`'s mount branch. The claim is the behaviour under guard.
- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1133` — `updateVdom()` parks every update while `!vnodeInitialized`; vdom updates are locked before the first render.
- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:147` — `afterSetVnodeInitialized` drains what parked, which is why the mutant still settles, only later.
- `test/playwright/unit/vdom/PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs` — the owning spec, already holding the #8082 controls this sits beside. Its `renderedText()` helper is the read this arm needs.

## The Fix

One arm in `PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs`: a child's `promiseUpdate()` requested after its container's first render collected settles **at the mount**, reading `pristine` — the tree that render carried — rather than waiting for the child's own follow-up render.

The arm's comment states that this is deliberate and names #18802 as the decision, so the next person to read it as a bug finds the ruling instead of re-deriving it.

No `src/` change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — an arm in `PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs` asserting the promise settles reading `pristine`, not merely that it settles.
- [ ] **AC-2** — mutation control recorded in the PR: with `afterSetMounted`'s claim made conditional on `!me.needsVdomUpdate`, the arm reds reading `late`. A draft asserting only settlement passes both ways and is therefore not acceptable.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the existing arms in that file stay green, including the two #8082 controls at `:234` and `:265`.
- [ ] **AC-4** — full `unit` suite green.

## Out of Scope

- Any `src/` change. #18802 is decided; this records the decision, it does not revisit it.
- The **re-parenting** scenario — an existing vnode unmounted and remounted across a long round trip. That is #18802's reopen trigger and belongs in e2e.
- `Workspace.mjs`'s use of `promiseUpdate` rather than `mountedPromise`. Migrating it is a real question and a separate one; nothing here depends on the answer.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not assert only that the promise settles.** Measured: that passes with the rejected change applied, because the drained follow-up cycle settles it 105 ms later. The arm must read what the caller reads at settle time.
- ⛔ **Do not write it as a defect arm.** It guards a contract deliberately kept. An arm phrased as "the caller sees the stale tree" invites a future author to 'fix' it — the comment has to carry the decision.

## Related

- #18782 / PR #18787 — the settle-timing guarantee whose one documented exception this pins
- #18817 — closed the same day; the other half of the same premise failure

* test(vdom): the mount's settle of an already-parked promise gets a unit guard (#18820)

A mount claims and settles everything parked on the component, so a
promiseUpdate() asked for after the mounting render collected reads the tree
that render carried. That is the one documented exception to the
settle-timing guarantee, and consumers depend on it: dock Workspace awaits
an UNMOUNTED host's promiseUpdate() purely to learn that it mounted.

Removing that claim was proposed, implemented two different ways, and
rejected. Until now the only thing in the repository that noticed was a
component arm reached through a cold boot, a saved-workspace URL, a recovery
button and a second window — which reads as a workstation-adoption test, so
reddening it tells nobody which contract they broke.

The arm asserts the READING at settle time, not that the promise settled. A
drained follow-up cycle settles it either way, roughly 100ms later, so a
settles-eventually assertion passes with the claim removed and guards
nothing — measured: 2ms reading `pristine` intact, 105ms reading `late` with
the claim conditional. Its comment carries the decision, so the next reader
who takes it for a bug finds the ruling instead of re-deriving it.

No src changes.
